content: 1. Trimalleolar fractures involve the fracture of all three malleoli of the ankle: the medial, lateral, and posterior malleoli. 2. Fractures of the lower leg can occur in unspecified parts, classified under code S82.9. 3. Dislocations, sprains, and strains of the knee joint and its associated ligaments are categorized under S83. 4. Dislocation of the patella (S83.0) refers to the displacement of the kneecap from its normal position. 5. Dislocation of the knee (S83.1) involves the misalignment of the tibiofemoral joint. 6. A current tear of the meniscus (S83.2) refers to damage to the cartilage that cushions the knee joint. 7. A current tear of the articular cartilage of the knee (S83.3) involves damage to the smooth cartilage covering the ends of bones in the knee joint. 8. Sprains and strains involving the fibular or tibial collateral ligaments of the knee (S83.4) refer to injuries to the stabilizing ligaments on the sides of the knee. 9. Sprains and strains involving the anterior or posterior cruciate ligaments of the knee (S83.5) involve injuries to the ligaments that stabilize the knee in the front and back. 10. Sprains and strains of other or unspecified parts of the knee (S83.6) refer to injuries to structures in the knee that are not specifically identified. 11. Injuries to multiple structures of the knee (S83.7) involve damage to more than one anatomical component of the knee joint. 12. Nerve injuries at the lower leg level (S84) involve trauma to the peripheral nerves in the lower leg. 13. Blood vessel injuries at the lower leg level (S85) refer to trauma affecting the vascular structures in the lower leg. 14. Muscle and tendon injuries at the lower leg level (S86) involve damage to the soft tissues responsible for movement and stability. 15. Crushing injuries of the lower leg (S87) result from significant compressive forces causing damage to the tissues. 16. Traumatic amputation of the lower leg (S88) refers to the loss of the lower leg due to severe trauma. 17. Other and unspecified injuries of the lower leg (S89) include injuries that do not fall into specific categories. 18. Superficial injuries of the ankle and foot (S90) involve damage to the skin or subcutaneous tissues. 19. Open wounds of the ankle and foot (S91) refer to injuries where the skin is broken, exposing underlying tissues. 20. Fractures of the foot, excluding the ankle (S92), include specific fractures such as: Fracture of the calcaneus (S92.0), the heel bone. Fracture of the talus (S92.1), a bone in the ankle joint. Fracture of other tarsal bones (S92.2), which are part of the midfoot. Fracture of the metatarsal bones (S92.3), including Jones fractures, which occur at the base of the fifth metatarsal. Fracture of the great toe (S92.4). Fracture of other toes (S92.5). Multiple fractures of the foot (S92.7). Unspecified fractures of the foot (S92.9). 21. Dislocations, sprains, and strains of the joints and ligaments at the ankle and foot level (S93) include: Dislocation of the ankle joint (S93.0). Dislocation of toes (S93.1). Rupture of ligaments at the ankle and foot level (S93.2). Dislocation of other or unspecified parts of the foot (S93.3). Sprains and strains of the ankle (S93.4). Sprains and strains of the toes (S93.5), including injuries to interphalangeal and metatarsophalangeal joints (e.g., turf toe). Sprains and strains of other or unspecified parts of the foot (S93.6). 22. Nerve injuries at the ankle and foot level (S94) involve trauma to the peripheral nerves in this region. 23. Blood vessel injuries at the ankle and foot level (S95) refer to trauma affecting the vascular structures in the ankle and foot. 24. Muscle and tendon injuries at the ankle and foot level (S96) involve damage to the soft tissues responsible for movement and stability. 25. Crushing injuries of the ankle and foot (S97) result from significant compressive forces causing damage to the tissues. 26. Traumatic amputation of the ankle and foot (S98) refers to the loss of these structures due to severe trauma. 27. Other and unspecified injuries of the ankle and foot (S99) include injuries that do not fall into specific categories. 28. Superficial injuries involving multiple body regions (T00) include abrasions, bruises, and other minor injuries affecting multiple areas. 29. Open wounds involving multiple body regions (T01) refer to injuries where the skin is broken in more than one area. 30. Fractures involving multiple body regions (T02) include breaks in bones across different anatomical areas. 31. Dislocations, sprains, and strains involving multiple body regions (T03) refer to injuries affecting joints and ligaments in various areas. 32. Crushing injuries involving multiple body regions (T04) result from compressive forces causing damage to tissues in multiple areas. 33. Traumatic amputations involving multiple body regions (T05) refer to the loss of body parts in more than one area due to severe trauma. 34. Other injuries involving multiple body regions, not elsewhere classified (T06), include injuries that do not fit into specific categories. 35. Unspecified multiple injuries (T07) refer to trauma affecting multiple areas without specific classification. 36. Fractures of the spine at an unspecified level (T08) involve breaks in the vertebrae without precise localization. 37. Other injuries of the spine and trunk at an unspecified level (T09) include: Superficial injuries of the trunk (T09.0). Open wounds of the trunk (T09.1). Dislocations, sprains, and strains of unspecified joints and ligaments of the trunk (T09.2). Injury of the spinal cord at an unspecified level (T09.3). Injury of unspecified nerves, spinal nerve roots, and plexuses of the trunk (T09.4). Injury of unspecified muscles and tendons of the trunk (T09.5). Traumatic amputation of the trunk at an unspecified level (T09.6). Other specified injuries of the trunk (T09.8). Unspecified injuries of the trunk (T09.9). 38. Fractures of the upper limb at an unspecified level (T10) involve breaks in the bones of the arm without precise localization. 39. Other injuries of the upper limb at an unspecified level (T11) include trauma to the arm that is not specifically classified. 40. Fractures of the lower limb at an unspecified level (T12) involve breaks in the bones of the leg without precise localization. 41. Other injuries of the lower limb at an unspecified level (T13) include trauma to the leg that is not specifically classified. 42. Injuries of unspecified body regions (T14) include: Superficial injuries (T14.0), such as abrasions, blisters, bruises, contusions, hematomas, and injuries from superficial foreign bodies or nonvenomous insect bites. Open wounds (T14.1), including animal bites, cuts, lacerations, puncture wounds, and open wounds with penetrating foreign bodies. Fractures (T14.2) of unspecified body regions. Dislocations, sprains, and strains (T14.3) of unspecified body regions. Injuries to nerves (T14.4) of unspecified body regions. Injuries to blood vessels (T14.5) of unspecified body regions. Injuries to muscles and tendons (T14.6) of unspecified body regions. Crushing injuries and traumatic amputations (T14.7) of unspecified body regions. Other injuries (T14.8) of unspecified body regions. Unspecified injuries (T14.9).
